nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.medication: Humulin (insulin isophane 70 U/mL + insulin regular 30 U/mL)
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management is essential in CKD (NG203 recommends optimal glucose control).

medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor creatinine & potassium after 1‑2 weeks, then every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: First‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with hypertension or ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol (NG203).
BP target <140/90 mmHg in CKD; CCBs are recommended adjuncts (NG203).

medications.purpose: Treatment of iron‑deficiency anaemia in CKD
medications.nice_justification: CKD‑related anaemia management includes iron supplementation (NG203).

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: Statin therapy is recommended for all CKD patients (NG203).

medications.dose: 1 tablet PO once daily (titrate to maintain HCO₃⁻ ≥ 22 mmol/L)
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L, then review
medications.purpose: Correct metabolic acidosis common in eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises oral bicarbonate when serum HCO₃⁻ <22 mmol/L.

medications.duration: Until PTH target achieved; then review every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: CKD‑MBD treatment with active vitamin D is recommended in stage 5 (NG203).

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily (titrate up to 80 mg BID as needed)
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate to volume status, review electrolytes monthly
medications.purpose: Hypertension and volume control; replace thiazide which is ineffective at eGFR < 30
medications.nice_justification: Loop diuretics are preferred for BP control in CKD with eGFR < 30 (NG203).

interactions_checked.action: Monitor for muscle pain; CK if symptomatic.
Take ferrous sulfate at least 2 hours apart from bicarbonate.

interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ within 1‑2 weeks of initiation, then monthly.

interactions_checked.action: Check Na⁺, K⁺, Mg²⁺ after dose changes.

contraindications.reason: eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis (NG203 contraindication).
Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention (NG203 contraindication).
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain if needed.

contraindications.reason: Dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalaemia and AKI risk (NG203).
contraindications.alternative: Continue ACE‑I alone; do not add ARB.

contraindications.reason: eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m² – not indicated per NG203 TA775.
contraindications.alternative: None; avoid SGLT2 inhibitor at this renal function.

assumptions_warnings: Serum bicarbonate level not provided – assumed <22 mmol/L for sodium bicarbonate initiation.
Calcium, phosphate, PTH, 25‑OH vitamin D levels not available – calcitriol to be started after labs confirm secondary hyperparathyroidism.
Lipid profile and QRISK score not available – atorvastatin started as CKD is a CV risk equivalent; LFTs to be checked before initiation.
Serum potassium not documented – baseline K⁺ required before starting calcitriol and after any diuretic change.
Blood pressure readings not provided – assumed uncontrolled given three antihypertensives; furosemide added and HCTZ to be discontinued.
Allergy status not documented – verify no statin or vitamin D intolerance before prescribing.
treatment_summary: The plan continues essential ACE‑I, CCB, insulin and iron therapy, adds atorvastatin for CV risk reduction, introduces sodium bicarbonate and calcitriol to address metabolic acidosis and CKD‑MBD (pending relevant labs), and replaces hydrochlorothiazide with furosemide for hypertension/volume control given eGFR 11.5. All additions follow NICE NG203 recommendations, with monitoring of electrolytes, liver function, lipid profile, bone‑mineral parameters, and blood pressure. Contraindicated agents (metformin, chronic NSAIDs, ARBs, SGLT2 inhibitors) are avoided.
